title: DECISION: Use receivedAt (server timestamp) instead of sentAt in message display
description: Message timestamps displayed to user come from receivedAt (server's local clock) not sentAt (peer-supplied claim). Rationale: sentAt is unverified and the peer's clock may be skewed. receivedAt represents the actual order of message arrival and cannot be spoofed (it's generated after Tailscale auth, inside kithd). Aligns with the trust boundary: peer message content is untrusted; reception timestamp is local fact.
